---
title: 8.1 Limits of Sequences of Numbers
subtitle: Finding a Sequence's Formula; Exercises 13-22
output: pdf_document
---

In Exercises 13-22, find a formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.

13. The sequence $1, -1, 1, -1, 1, \ldots$

> 1's with alternating signs, beginning with 1.

$$
a_n = (-1)^{n + 1}, n \ge 1
$$

14. The sequence $-1, 1, -1, 1, -1, \ldots$

> 1's with alternating signs, beginning with -1.

$$
a_n = (-1)^n, n \ge 1
$$

15. The sequence $1, -4, 9, -16, 25, \ldots$

> Squares of the positive integers, with alternating signs.

$$
a_n = (-1)^{n + 1}(n^2), n \ge 1
$$

16. The sequence $1, -\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{9}, -\frac{1}{16}, \frac{1}{25}, \cdots$

> Reciprocals of squares of the positive integers, with alternating signs.

$$
a_n = (-1)^{n + 1}\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)^2, n \ge 1
$$

17. The sequence $0, 3, 8 ,15, 24, \ldots$

> Squares of the positive integers diminished by 1.

$$
a_n = n^2-1, n \ge 1
$$

18. The sequence $-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, \ldots$

> Integers beginning with -3.

$$
a_n = n, n \ge -3
$$

19. The sequence $1, 5, 9, 13, 17, \ldots$

> Every other odd positive integer.

$$
a_n = 4n-3
$$

20. The sequence $2, 6, 10, 14, 18, \ldots$

> Every other even positive integer

$$
a_n = 4n-2
$$

21. The sequence $1, 0, 1, 0, 1, \ldots$

> Alternating 1's and 0's.

$$
a_n = \frac{1 - (-1)^n}{2}
$$

22. The sequence $0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, \ldots$

> Each positive integer repeated.

$$
a_n = \frac{2n - 1 + (-1)^n}{4}
$$
